text:
tana: heads up — after merging runtime PR 7f3a2c we see ~15% per-token latency regression on small-batch (1-4) workloads. nsys traces attached below, pinging eng-runtime to triage

miguel: saw this on rtx-a100 pool too. repro'd with minimal client. timeline shows shader switch spikes interleaved with KV reads.

sara: quick nsys summary i pulled: 'kv_read' avg increased 0.9ms -> 1.6ms per call; total launch count up ~30%. also more cudaLaunch calls clustered around token boundaries.

jon: can you paste the nsys timeline snippet or a perfetto link? want to eyeball kernel handoffs.

tana: nsys command i ran:
```
nsys profile --output /tmp/trace.ns --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --unified-experimental true 
./bin/redwood-serving --model small --batch 1 --seq 256 --iters 200
```
perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (first bad run)

perf-bot: profile uploaded: s3://redwood-profiles/2112223334/7f3a2c-after.ns (tags: eng-runtime, bisect) :white_check_mark:

miguel: hypothesis: kernel selector started probing extra codepaths for quantized kernels in the hot path. looks like we do an extra probe launch per shard which amplifies at small batch.

sara: nvprof confirms repeated cuLaunchKernel entries for 'quant_select_probe' at higher frequency in bad trace. batching heuristic change in that PR? it probes per request instead of once per model config.

jon: plan: git bisect between good commit a1b2c3 and bad 7f3a2c. use an automated bisect script that runs a tiny inference and checks median token latency. i'll kick it off on gpu-bisect-02.

tana: bisect commands i'm using:
```
git bisect start 7f3a2c a1b2c3
git bisect run ./tools/prof-bisect.sh --repro 'python -m tests.small_infer --batch 1 --seq 256 --iters 100 --warmup 10'
```
(the script uploads nsys traces and returns 0 if median latency < 88ms)

perf-bot: started bisect job #432 on gpu-bisect-02. will post step traces as they complete. ETA ~45m.

miguel: also try this quick toggles: REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0 and REDWOOD_KERNEL_PROBE=0 to see impact. if disabling prefetch collapses the spike it's kv ordering.

sara: quick test results from my VM:
- before PR (a1b2c3): median token lat = 82ms
- after PR (7f3a2c): median token lat = 95ms
- after PR + REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0: median token lat = 84ms
So disabling prefetch nearly recovers the baseline. strong signal toward KV warmup ordering.

jon: filing issue INF-578 with traces and nvprof outputs. if bisect points to the PR we revert the probe-in-hotpath change and look at moving probing to background thread or cache result per model.

tana: thanks all — i'll wait for bisect artifacts and then run before/after nsys diff (perfetto comparison). will post final writeup in this thread when bisect finishes. :eyes:
